newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia wants Ventspils port in EU corridor.
newsitem.headline: Latvia wants Ventspils port in EU corridor.

text.p: Latvia wants to get its Ventspils port, the largest on the Baltic Sea, included as part of a European Union (EU) transport corridor running between Helsinki and Warsaw, the transport ministry said on Monday.
Ventspils oil terminal is already a main outlet for Russian crude oil but there is also a busy commercial port there.
Being part of an EU transport corridor, Latvia would get EU aid to upgrade its port facilities and improve communications.
"We believe that this will generate more transit flows," Latvian transport ministry strategic planning department deputy head Vigo Legzdinsh told a news conference.
Legzdinsh said the Baltic state has sent its proposals to Brussels to get Ventspils included on the Helsinki-Warsaw route, known as EU corridor number one.
"The basic idea is to join our biggest port Ventspils to the trans-European network by widening the Helsinki-Warsaw corridor," Legzdinsh added.
In 1996 Latvian ports registered some 45 million tonnes turnover, mainly Russian raw material exports.
Ventspils had the biggest throughput by far in the region, registering turnover of 18 million tonnes.
"The national transport priority in Latvia is an East-West link, connecting C.I.S. and Latvian ports," Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said.
But Latvia still needs Russia to name the route to Ventspils as one of its priorities.
"Russia does not say no, but it has not said yes either," Lagzdinsh said.
A first reaction from Brussels on the Latvian proposal is expected on February 20, transport officials said.
